idiom_name: Stream.iterate(seed, hasNext, next) / IntStream as the unfold + reduce as the fold
implementation_notes: The JDK's lazy Stream pipeline is the library realization: Stream.iterate(seed, hasNext, next) or IntStream.range/iterate is the coalgebra and Stream.reduce (or IntStream.reduce) is the algebra; because intermediate operations are lazy, the two run interleaved element by element and no intermediate List is ever built - the pipeline is the fused recursion. Prefer the primitive streams and the three-argument iterate (Java 9) for state-dependent termination, and use takeWhile to stop an otherwise unbounded unfold. The explicit loop remains the choice on hot paths where boxing and lambda dispatch dominate.
pitfalls: Stream.reduce requires an associative operator for well-defined parallel results; a non-associative algebra silently changes value under parallel(), so keep the pipeline sequential or use the loop.
An unbounded Stream.iterate without the Java 9 predicate or a limit() hangs forever - the generator must own its termination condition.
Boxed Integer/Long elements allocate on every step; use IntStream/LongStream/DoubleStream for numeric unfolds.

variants.name: Hand-written fused loop (boxing-free, deterministic)
variants.idiom_name: for/while loop with a local accumulator and an explicit seed step
variants.implementation_notes: The same fusion without streams: a loop that computes the next seed and immediately combines it with a local accumulator, keeping the algebra and the coalgebra as named static methods. It avoids boxing entirely, is trivially profiled, and its evaluation order is fixed, which matters when the algebra is not associative or the pipeline would otherwise be tempted into parallel(). Choose it for hot numeric work and for codebases that deliberately avoid streams; choose the stream variant when the generator already is an Iterable, file or collection, where laziness comes for free with the API.
pitfalls: Hand-rolled drivers are duplicated per shape, so the combine step should stay a named static method rather than inline arithmetic three times in three classes.
Folding left changes the result for non-associative or non-commutative algebras; document the direction the loop implies.
Widening and overflow: long accumulators wrap silently - use Math.multiplyHigh/addExact or BigInteger where the seed range is not controlled.
